solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quietly utter joke

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for playing quietly
utter and rank both mean complete, out-and-out, as in a rank amateur

explanation.surface: Someone muttering a joke under their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like a verb (to speak) but works as the adjective meaning total.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical joke or trick played on someone is called a prank.

clue.text: TV character represented on stamp — apt!

indicators.note: represented hints at presenting again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A television favourite appears on a postage stamp, which seems fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: He is the British children's TV postman from Greendale, so a stamp is doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheerful village postie with a black-and-white cat is a long-running British children's TV figure.

clue.text: Trouble? A spot, not tons

indicators.note: not means the following item is left out of the word before it

parts.note: a dot is a small spot

explanation.surface: A question whether a little spot is trouble, if not a heavy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing, is a form of trouble.

clue.text: A quiz finally entering knockout round with small noisy buzzers

indicators.note: entering means the letters go inside the abbreviation for a knockout

parts.note: KO is the standard boxing abbreviation for knockout

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A quiz show's knockout round with contestants on small loud buzzers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzers' suggests quiz-show buttons, which fits the surface, but means the hummed toy instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: These little toy instruments make a buzzing sound when you hum into them.

clue.text: One replacing a DIY essential for occupant of flats

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter takes the place of another letter in the word that follows

parts.note: sandpaper is a basic do-it-yourself tool for smoothing wood
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone swapping out a key piece of home-improvement kit for a tenant in a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: The second A of the abrasive paper becomes I. 'Flats' are not apartments but mudflats, the low shores where wading birds feed.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird feeds on mudflats and shorelines, so it is a resident of flats in that sense.

clue.text: Club seals and we'd get hides

indicators.note: hides means the answer is concealed within the run of words before it

explanation.surface: A club with which you'd catch seals and take their skins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' looks like seal skins, fitting the clubbing image, but signals the concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: This lofted iron is the golf club made for bunker shots.

clue.text: Woman I grumble about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to moan is to grumble

explanation.surface: A woman complains about having something to grumble about.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, as with the biblical mother-in-law of Ruth.

clue.text: Relieve picket, holding the rear up

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: a pale is a fence stake, a picket

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the tail is the rear end

explanation.surface: A striker on the picket line raising the back of something to ease it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picket' suggests a strike line; here it is a fence post (PALE).
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or symptoms without curing them is to make them more bearable.

clue.text: Distribute supporting navigation guide for groundbreaking device

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the first piece below the second

parts.note: the Plough, the Big Dipper star group, helps navigators find north
to share is to distribute

explanation.surface: Handing out a navigational aid that backs an innovative invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groundbreaking' suggests innovative but means literally breaking soil.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the cutting blade of a farm implement that turns the soil.

clue.text: Aid for landing fish after a little resistance

indicators.note: after means the fish comes following the first letter
a little of the word means just its opening letter

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Something to help land a catch when the fish puts up some fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers wind in a catch on this spool attached to the rod.

clue.text: In favour of cutting Liszt's 3rd and 4th with old musician's direction

indicators.note: cutting means the next piece slices into the pair of letters, sitting between them
names the third and fourth letters of the composer's name, the middle pair

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for a motion
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: Support slicing into some Liszt along with an old musical marking.
explanation.walkthrough: The third and fourth letters of LISZT'S are S and Z; FOR goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Italian instruction in a score telling the player to accent a note sharply.

clue.text: Free and easy

definitions.meaning: free here means let go or unconfined, as an animal running at large
easy here means relaxed or slack, as in a garment that hangs comfortably

explanation.surface: The stock phrase for a relaxed, informal manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idiom, but it splits into two separate definitions joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unconfined (an animal on the run) and slack or relaxed.

clue.text: Simple code that cannot encrypt bid, for example

definitions.text: Simple code that cannot encrypt bid, for example

parts.words: Simple code that cannot encrypt bid, for example
parts.note: script reflected left to right is an easy cipher, but the letters b-i-d look the same when flipped, since b and d swap

explanation.surface: A basic cipher that fails on a short word like an auction offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Flip 'bid' in a mirror and b and d swap places and shapes, so the word reads unchanged and nothing is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo-style backwards script is a classic simple cipher, and some words survive it unchanged.

clue.text: Unhappy teetotaller opening beer and lager for refreshment

indicators.note: opening means the abstainer's letters cut open the mixed drink letters
refreshment suggests making new again, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: TT is shorthand for a teetotaller, one who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A sad non-drinker cracking open beer and lager to quench thirst.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfortunate or to be lamented is an unhappy matter, as in an unhappy event.

clue.text: Some pages flutter around street, discarded mostly

indicators.note: around means the wager wraps the following letters

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet in British usage
a road is a street

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: to shed is to discard

explanation.surface: Loose pages blowing around the street, mostly thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' suggests pages fluttering but is British slang for a modest wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A large-format newspaper, traditionally the serious press, consists of several pages.

clue.text: Horse and trap's return is imminent

indicators.note: return means the letters formed by the horse and the trap are taken in the opposite direction

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
a gin is a trap for catching animals, a gin-trap

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn trap is about to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse and trap' suggests a carriage; here horse is H (heroin) and trap is GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand in time, about to happen, is near or close by.

clue.text: Hyper? Arrange sedative and R&R

indicators.note: arrange tells us to put the letters of the following words into a new order

parts.note: rest and recuperation, written with two Rs

explanation.surface: An overexcited person is told to sort out a sedative and some rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hyper?' looks like a description of an excitable person but means one who hypes, a promoter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hypes a product promotes it, which is what an advertising person does; the question mark flags the coinage.

clue.text: Look forward to present after studies

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: to eye something is to study it
to front a show is to present it

explanation.surface: Looking ahead to a gift after exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look forward to present' reads as anticipating a gift, but the definition ends at 'forward'.
explanation.definitionFit: This parade-ground order tells soldiers to face straight ahead.

clue.text: Line up digger capturing hydrogen in small tunnel

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a row is a line

indicators.note: capturing means the burrower encloses the element symbol

parts.note: a mole digs tunnels
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Arranging diggers excavating hydrogen inside a narrow tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm's burrow is a small passage, and in physics a hypothetical space-time shortcut.

clue.text: Wind instrument contributing to atmospheric records?

definitions.text: Wind instrument contributing to atmospheric records?

parts.words: Wind instrument contributing to atmospheric records?
parts.note: not a flute or oboe but a gauge measuring wind speed, whose readings go into weather records

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind instrument' suggests music and 'records' suggests albums with atmosphere; both point to meteorology instead.
explanation.definitionFit: This device gauges wind speed, so it literally is an instrument for wind, feeding weather data.

clue.text: Feature of landscape gardens comprising two hectares

indicators.note: two tells us the unit symbol appears twice in a row

parts.note: ha is the symbol for hectare, a land measure

explanation.surface: A garden landscape feature that occupies a couple of hectares.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall, common on English country estates, that keeps livestock out without blocking the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken boundary ditch is a classic element of eighteenth-century English landscaped parks.

clue.text: Briefly remain with relative in stable condition

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to stay is to remain
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A short hospital stay with a family member, in stable condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of equilibrium where nothing changes is a steady, unchanging state.

clue.text: Wretchedly moan often: this is a fellow who certainly did

indicators.note: wretchedly suggests something in a sorry state, signalling that the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who moans endlessly and miserably, and a figure who did exactly that.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to the clue's first words: this Shakespeare hero moaned wretchedly and often, turning misanthrope.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's title character becomes a bitter, complaining misanthrope after his generosity is betrayed.

clue.text: Cue imparting spin on for example brown

indicators.note: spin turns things around, so the letters of these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A snooker cue putting spin on the brown ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the brown is a ball and a cue is the stick; here cue means a prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle prompt or reminder to do something is a hint or signal.

clue.text: Leading couples in Strictly episodes must be in this

definitions.text: Leading couples in Strictly episodes must be in this

indicators.note: the leading pair of letters from each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Top dancing pairs on the TV show have to keep in time.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom-dancing show; ST from Strictly and EP from episodes.
explanation.definitionFit: Partners dancing together must move in time with each other, in unison.

clue.text: Cheers and jeers largely disapproved of

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: boos are jeers from a crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd's mixed cheering and booing mostly showing disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like applause but means thanks (TA), a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by social custom is frowned upon, banned by convention.

clue.text: Pancake falls to earth once tossed

parts.note: drops means comes down to the ground

indicators.note: tossed, like a pancake flipped in the pan, tells us the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A pancake hits the floor after being flipped once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' fits the pancake surface but is the anagram signal on ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: This small thick Scottish griddle cake is also called a Scotch pancake.

clue.text: Even pieces from gorilla can constitute a work of art

indicators.note: even pieces means the letters in even positions, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A gorilla's bits could make up an artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting done in oils is called an oil, a work of fine art.

clue.text: Before Christ impressed Mark, providing an example for followers

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
CE, Common Era, is the dating convention used in place of AD, in the year of Christ
a dent is a mark pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: A religious-sounding statement that something before Christ left a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before Christ' suggests BC; instead 'Christ' stands for the Common Era, the secular name for the years once counted from his birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A previous case or decision serves as a model that later decisions follow.

clue.text: Scottish League One team's first in division

parts.note: SPL was the Scottish Premier League, Scotland's top football division
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A Scottish football side's leading player in the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'League One' looks like a division name; here it splits into SPL plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift or separation into parts is a dividing, as in a party split.
